prompt: Joe decided that he would try to make some extra money by raking the leaves in his neighbors' yards. Joe figured he would need approximately seven bags per yard in which to collect the leaves. The bags are sold 10 to a box, and Joe is planning on raking 14 yards. How many boxes of bags must he buy?

solutions.title: Count bags, then boxes
solutions.body:
Bags needed: $7 \times 14 = 98$. Boxes: $98 \div 10 = 9.8$, so 9 boxes (90 bags) are not enough; he must buy **10** boxes.

**Answer: 10 boxes**

solutions.title: Check 9 vs 10 boxes
solutions.body:
9 boxes hold 90 bags, which covers only $90 \div 7 \approx 12.9$ yards — fewer than 14. 10 boxes hold 100 bags, enough for $14 \times 7 = 98$.

**Answer: 10 boxes**

prompt: Heather noticed that the high temperature on October 21st was 66 degrees, the high temperature on October 26th was 63 degrees and the high temperature on October 31st was 60 degrees. It appears that the high temperatures on every fifth day are forming an arithmetic sequence. If this sequence were to continue, on what date would the high temperature be 33 degrees?

solutions.title: Count the steps
solutions.body:
The temperature drops 3 degrees every 5 days. From 60° (October 31) to 33° is a drop of $27$ degrees, i.e. $27 \div 3 = 9$ steps, which is $9 \times 5 = 45$ days after October 31.

November has 30 days, so 30 days after October 31 is November 30, and 15 more days is **December 15**.

**Answer: December 15**

solutions.title: List the sequence
solutions.body:
Oct 31: 60, Nov 5: 57, Nov 10: 54, Nov 15: 51, Nov 20: 48, Nov 25: 45, Nov 30: 42, Dec 5: 39, Dec 10: 36, Dec 15: 33.

**Answer: December 15**

prompt: Lou promised himself he would exercise at least four days of every calendar week (every Sunday through Saturday period). If Lou never wants to skip exercising on consecutive days within a calendar week, and he exercises exactly four days out of the seven, how many different workout schedules are possible for a calendar week?

solutions.title: List the skipped days
solutions.body:
Lou skips exactly 3 of the 7 days, and no two skipped days may be next to each other. Write the days as S, M, T, W, R, F, Q (Sunday … Saturday) and list the skipped triples:

- Starting with S: (S,T,R), (S,T,F), (S,T,Q), (S,W,F), (S,W,Q), (S,R,Q) — 6
- Starting with M: (M,W,F), (M,W,Q), (M,R,Q) — 3
- Starting with T: (T,R,Q) — 1

Total: $6 + 3 + 1 = 10$.

**Answer: 10**

solutions.title: Gaps between workout days
solutions.body:
Line up the 4 workout days: X X X X. They create 5 gaps (before, between, after). Each skipped day goes into a different gap so that no two skipped days touch. Choosing 3 of the 5 gaps: $\binom{5}{3} = 10$.

**Answer: 10**
